title: Bad handwriting
translation: If your handwriting is bad, go ahead and write your letters anyway. That's fine. Getting someone else to write them because yours looks ugly is just tiresome.
original: {手|て}の{悪|わろ}き{人|ひと}の、{憚|はばか}らず{文|ふみ}かきちらすはよし。
{見苦|みぐる}しとて{人|ひと}に{書|か}かするはうるさし。
literal: A person whose hand is bad writing letters freely without hesitation is good.
Having someone else write, saying it is unsightly, is tiresome.

notes.text: {手|て}: handwriting (see section 1). Good handwriting was a real social asset at court, and people did have others write their letters for them.

A false friend: here 'tiresome, irritating, too much'. Modern うるさい is mostly 'noisy'; here it is only 'tiresome'. Kenkō prefers honest bad handwriting to borrowed good handwriting, which fits section 150.
